text:
You need someone who can systematically search public property websites across the United States and build a clean list of public metadata sources for residential properties.

I’m Mina Castellan, and I have 5 years of experience in data analysis, data cleaning, data visualization, and list-building work using SQL, Excel, Power BI, and Google Sheets. This type of research-heavy project fits well with my background because I’m comfortable organizing large amounts of information, checking details carefully, and keeping data structured so it stays usable as the list grows.

One project that is especially relevant is the Sales KPI dashboard for Marlowe Furniture. I built one Power BI report on a star-schema model to replace 14 separate Excel sales reports. That consolidation reduced monthly close reporting from 3 days to 4 hours. While that project was focused on reporting rather than property research, it shows the way I approach work: gather scattered sources, clean and structure the data, and turn it into something consistent and easy to maintain.

For your project, I would focus on finding public state and county property data sources, organizing the findings in Excel or Google Sheets, and making sure the list is clear enough for you to keep expanding. I can also work with ongoing communication so you can review progress and confirm that the search direction matches what you need. Since you already have a reference list started, I can use that as a guide and help continue building it in the same format.

I’m detail-oriented and comfortable with repetitive research tasks as long as accuracy matters, which is important for a project like this where public metadata sources may vary by state, county, and website structure. I’d be glad to help you build a dependable reference list that you can continue using.

What format would you like the final list to follow for each source: county/state name, website URL, property data type, and any notes on access or metadata?
